evidence.claim: Cash App's notice says it explains what data it collects, what it does with it, when and why it shares it, how long it keeps it, how it secures it, and what choices you have.

In a supplement for residents of certain U.S. states, Cash App says that while it does not sell personal information as commonly understood, it 'shares' personal information for advertising using cookies and similar technologies. The supplement says it does not apply to information about Cash App customers using its financial products (covered by a separate U.S. Consumer Privacy Notice), so its reach for app users is not established.

Cash App says it may share information with advertising partners and, starting on or after Feb 9, 2026, its commerce media network may use data about your activity (such as shopping history, app browsing behavior, card transactions and general location) to show personalized ads for other brands outside Cash App, and may share interest categories, masked identifiers and device data with advertising technology providers.
For the commerce media network ad activity, users can opt out (or opt in where the law requires) in Account & Settings > Privacy.

In its state-law supplement, Cash App says it may ask you to confirm a deletion request before deleting personal information, and that these rights do not apply to personal information governed by the GLBA.

Cash App says its commerce media network may use data about your activity to show personalized ads for other brands outside Cash App (from Feb 9, 2026), with an opt-out in Account & Settings > Privacy. A state-law supplement says it does not sell personal information as commonly understood but 'shares' it for advertising; that supplement excludes Cash App customers' financial-product data.

Exodus Privacy static analysis of version 5.16.1 (report dated Sept. 15, 2025) found code signatures for 3 known tracker SDK(s): AppsFlyer (analytics), Bugsnag (crash reporting), Google Firebase Analytics (analytics). A signature shows the SDK is present, not what data it sends.
